deep_dive.title: VTC-AUDIT: An Interventional Reliability Audit for Visual-Token Compression under Paired Image Shifts
deep_dive.abstract: Visual-token compression is usually evaluated by clean accuracy and efficiency, but these averages do not reveal failures that compression introduces under an image shift where the uncompressed model stays correct. We introduce VTC-AUDIT, which estimates this incremental risk only on pairs where the full model is correct on both images and the compressed model is correct on the clean image. The four arms then cross two binary choices: which image selects the retained token positions, and which image supplies the visual features. We audit three open 8-9B vision-language models on four tasks and eight pre-specified shifts. We evaluate two training-free compressors---hard-pruning DivPrune and prune-and-merge ApET---at a matched 25% retained-position budget, producing 708,000 inference records. Reselecting positions on the shifted image, rather than reusing the clean-image positions, raises the failure rate in all six model-compressor settings. The increase is 3.04-9.60 percentage points for DivPrune and 2.05-4.20 percentage points for ApET, with every 95% interval above zero. Repeating the audit on a separately resampled second manifest reproduces all six increases. In a pooled monitor audit across the four benchmarks, support Jaccard instability fails the practical AUROC criterion of 0.65 in all six settings, whereas clean compressed-model uncertainty clears it. Thus, support turnover is a weak ranking signal under the audited benchmark mixture, while clean compressed-model uncertainty is substantially more informative. These results suggest that future visual-token compression evaluations should report conditional reliability alongside clean accuracy and efficiency.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Visual-token compression is normally judged by clean accuracy, hiding failures under image shift; VTC-AUDIT measures incremental risk on paired images and audits pruning and prune-and-merge compressors across three 8-9B VLMs.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 视觉令牌压缩通常仅用干净图像的准确率与效率来评估，这会掩盖图像偏移下压缩新引入的失败。作者提出VTC-AUDIT，仅在全集模型对两图都正确、且压缩模型在干净图上正确的配对上估计增量风险，并交叉两种令牌位置选择与特征来源。他们在三个8-9B视觉语言模型、四个任务与八种预设偏移上审计DivPrune与ApET两类免训练压缩器。该审计揭示了压缩在分布偏移下的隐性风险，为压缩方法提供了更可靠的评估协议。

quick_skim.title: Training-Free Inference Acceleration for Video Large Language Models: Methods, Trade-offs, and Evaluation
quick_skim.abstract: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. We complement this analysis with quantitative evidence from prior studies and our own experiments under a shared evaluation setting to assess accuracy-latency trade-offs.
